description: PROPOSED (Discussion #49, alternative B: declared aggregation), NOT in the spec on main. `producer` is the second proposed strategy: the producer asserted `passed` by its own rules and consumers MUST NOT re-derive it from the graders. The row is q7 of the AgentEval .NET adapter's sample output (real AgentEval 0.43.0-beta CompositeEval run, no LLM): the exact grader passed, the required judge was skipped (`measurement: notMeasured`), and AgentEval's own composite verdict is `warn` -- a pass cannot rest on a required component that did not run -- so `passed` is false although the spec's default `all` over the scored graders would say true. Neither `all` nor `strict` describes that; `producer` does, and the native verdict stays in metadata.

agenteval.passed_semantics: Result.passed is AgentEval's own verdict (AND of Score.Passed over the case's top-level results); null-scored graders are not re-aggregated by this exporter

verdicts.label: warn
verdicts.summary: Required component(s) that did not run or could not attest their own pass: judge. A pass cannot rest on them, so the verdict is warn. Measured 1 of 2 component(s); 1 left out of the score (1 skipped or not measured, 0 inapplicable, 0 errored).
